key_insight: A deep neural network predicts noise figure in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers about 400× faster than a semi-quantum calculation framework, with 0.0015 dB mean absolute error.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate enables rapid exploration of amplifier designs targeting 20 dB gain and 0.3 dB noise figure.
method: Generate simulated parameter-to-noise-figure data using a semi-quantum framework.
Train an optimized deep neural network for rapid noise-figure prediction.
Use clustering to explore the parameter space and retrieve candidate design parameters.
evidence_signal: Evaluation against semi-quantum calculations reports about 400× lower computation time and 0.0015 dB mean absolute error on numerically simulated data.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based results; experimental validation and reliability outside the sampled parameter space remain unestablished.
paper_title: Deep-learning surrogate model for rapid quantum-noise computation in dual-pump fiber-optic phase-sensitive amplifiers
